US Credit Conditions
Integrates credit spreads, systemic-stress indicators, and private-credit growth signals to assess the prevailing US credit-conditions regime.

Regime Assessment:

  • Regime: Transitional / Fragile Balance
  • Regime Confidence Index: Medium Confidence
  • Stability: The regime is fragile.

Why This Regime:

  • High-weight tactical indicators show system-wide stress is at historical lows (5).
  • Medium-weight cyclical signals confirm funding environments remain within historical norms (2)(3).
  • Dynamic weighting prioritizes high-confidence stress data over lagging credit growth metrics.
  • We downweighted the Credit Spreads Signal (1) and Private Credit Impulse (4) due to low interpretation confidence.

Alignment & Tensions:

  • Systemic liquidity aligns with compressed investment grade spreads (2)(1).
  • Tensions exist between tactical risk-on shifts and weakening credit momentum (5)(4).
  • Neutral cyclical signals (3) act as a buffer against these tactical fluctuations.
  • Tensions do not overturn the call because systemic stress remains subdued.

Scenario Balance:

  • The dominant scenario is range-biased price paths supported by stable funding.
  • Primary upside risk is a shift to "Low Stress" if spreads compress further (2).
  • Primary downside risk is a regime flip to "Tightening" driven by HY OAS expansion (3).

What Would Change the Regime:

  • HY_OAS rising above 3.5% would invalidate the easy credit assumption (1).
  • Stress_z rising above -0.5 would signal a return to neutral or bearish stress levels (5).
  • A composite breach above 0.75 would indicate a transition to high financial stress (2).

Model Lineage

Visualisations below present upstream signal states and evidence context used to form the current silver market interpretation.

Credit Spreads Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given HY_OAS of 2.80% and IG_OAS of 0.75%, this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Compressed volatility, where the dominant risk is Trend continuation, not Regime shift.
  • The signal reflects an EASY credit regime, as the primary High Yield metric remains well below the lower volatility threshold (1).
  • Conviction Band: Low; Interpretation Confidence: Low Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Stable; Threshold Proximity: Far; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • HY < 3.5% defines abundant credit availability and low perceived default risk, supporting risk-on positioning (1).
  • HY increases > 50 bps over 3 months are required to signal a transition toward risk-off conditions (1).
  • High Yield (HY) components are prioritized over Investment Grade (IG) for determining cyclical sensitivity (1).
  • Credit Spreads Signal (Latest: 2026-05-31) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • Current HY_OAS (2.80%) is significantly below the 3.5% threshold for "EASY" classification (1).
  • IG_OAS has compressed to 0.75%, confirming broad-based stability in risk premia across the credit stack (1).
  • Momentum is stabilizing; spreads have declined from a temporary 2025 peak of 3.94% (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: HY_OAS rising above 3.5% or a 50 bps expansion within a 3-month window (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Continued risk-on environment supported by low default risk expectations.
  • Upside risk: Further spread compression if corporate profitability exceeds expectations.
  • Downside risk: Sudden liquidity shock causing bid-ask inflation and a regime flip.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months) based on the lead-indicator properties of credit for equity drawdowns (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Low, due to the absence of CSC z-score composite data.

Macro Relevance:

  • Dimension: Liquidity and Pricing.
  • Economic Mechanism: Easing financial conditions reduce borrowing costs, incentivizing capital expenditure and risk-taking (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.

Regime Context:

  • The EASY regime is persistent, having been maintained for two consecutive months following a recovery from 2025 volatility (1).
  • Direction of change: Stabilizing at low levels.

Model Limitations:

  • Bid-ask spread inflation during shocks can cause false regime flips (1).
  • Revision window cannot be assessed from provided content.

Data & References:

  • Credit Spreads Signal (Latest: 2026-05-31) (1).
  • Primary drivers: HY_OAS and IG_OAS levels (1).
  • External verification: ICE BofA HY Master II (H0A0) and US Corporate Master (C0A0).
Financial Stress Composite Signal

  • The signal remains in a Neutral regime at -0.609, showing recent movement toward the lower boundary of accommodative conditions. (1)
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Volatile; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • Composite values between -0.75 and 0.75 define the Neutral regime, suggesting financial conditions are near historical norms. (1)
  • STLFSI4 serves as a proxy for system-wide stress across funding and cross-asset markets. (1)
  • Yield curve inversion (T10Y2Y) measures stress driven by tight monetary policy relative to growth expectations. (1)
  • Financial Stress Composite Signal: Latest observation May 31, 2026. (1)

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the STLFSI4 (Z-score: -0.66), indicating subdued systemic liquidity strain. (1)
  • The T10Y2Y spread is positive (0.54), exerting downward pressure on the stress composite. (1)
  • Conditional Invalidation: A composite breach below -0.75 would trigger a "Low Stress" (risk-on) regime. (1)
  • Stability: The signal has fluctuated within the Neutral band for 36 months, exhibiting short-term volatility in 2026. (1)

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Persistence in Neutral regime as liquidity remains stable.
  • Upside risk: Transition to Low Stress triggered by further narrowing of credit spreads (HY OAS).
  • Downside risk: Shift toward High Stress if funding markets (STLFSI4) tighten abruptly.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months), as regime shifts reflect broader economic health.
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium, given the signal is currently in a non-trending Neutral state.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs systemic liquidity and credit risk premia dimensions. (1)
  • Implied mechanism: Low systemic strain currently facilitates stable corporate funding and moderate risk appetite. (1)
  • Cycle position: Not determined by methodology.

Regime Context:

  • Persistent Neutral regime; the signal has not breached stress thresholds since June 2023. (1)
  • Direction of change: Stabilising near the accommodative threshold after a brief spike in Q1 2026. (1)

Model Limitations:

  • Monthly resampling may miss intramonth volatility spikes in funding markets. (1)
  • Fixed thresholds may lag structural shifts in financial market architecture. (1)

Data & References:

  • Latest Data: STLFSI4 (-0.7621), HY_OAS (2.80), T10Y2Y (0.54) as of 2026-05-31. (1)

Credit Conditions Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given a Credit Conditions index of -0.15, supported by compressed BBB spreads (Z-score: -0.79) and moderate equity volatility (Z-score: 0.34), this setup aligns with Range-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Mean reversion, not Regime shift. (1)
  • The signal is currently in a persistent Neutral regime, characterized by funding environments within historical norms. (1)
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Stable; Threshold Proximity: Moderate; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • A composite index between -0.75 and 0.75 indicates a neutral funding environment with no strong directional bias. (1)
  • Standardized deviations (z-scores) of HY OAS, BBB OAS, and VIX drive the aggregate reading. (1)
  • Rising values signal a transition toward risk-off/slowdown, while falling values indicate risk-on/expansion. (1)
  • Credit Conditions Signal: Latest observation 2026-05-31. (1)

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the stabilization of credit spreads (HY and BBB) offset by slightly elevated VIX. (1)
  • Momentum has stabilized following a brief tightening impulse in early 2026. (1)
  • Internal tension exists between easing corporate spreads and a positive Z-score in equity volatility. (1)
  • Conditional Invalidation: An index breach of +0.75 would signal a transition to a Tightening regime. (1)
  • The signal has remained within the Neutral band for 20 consecutive months. (1)

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Continued neutral funding environment supports existing corporate financing structures.
  • Upside risk: A shift to the Easing regime triggered by a significant compression in equity volatility.
  • Downside risk: Tightening credit conditions triggered by a sharp widening in HY spreads.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months); the signal measures corporate funding environments across business cycles. (1)
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Medium; neutral regimes act as a baseline for other macro indicators.

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs the corporate funding environment and broad market risk appetite. (1)
  • Implies a stable transmission of liquidity to the real economy without immediate margin pressure. (1)
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Interacts with USD strength and credit supply metrics to confirm liquidity regimes. (1)

Regime Context:

  • The regime is persistent, having avoided a transition to "Tightening" despite recent volatility spikes. (1)
  • Direction of change: Stabilising at lower-neutral levels. (1)

Model Limitations:

  • Mixed data frequencies (weekly OAS vs daily VIX) can create temporary artifacts. (1)
  • VIX may reflect equity-specific risks rather than broad corporate credit fundamentals. (1)

Data & References:

  • Credit Conditions Signal (2026-05-31). (1)
  • Z_BBB (-0.79) and Z_VIX (0.34) are the most influential components for the current reading. (1)
  • USD Strength and Credit Supply metrics would improve cross-validation.
Private Credit Impulse Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given a Private Credit Impulse of 0.73 and a Z_TOTBKCR_ann6 of 0.73, this setup aligns with Transition-biased price paths and Normal volatility, where the dominant risk is Regime shift, not Trend continuation (1).
  • The signal has transitioned from an "Accelerating" regime to "Stable" as of May 2026, though it currently sits at the upper threshold of the transition zone (1).
  • Conviction Band: Low; Interpretation Confidence: Low Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: Yes. Signal Stability Assessment: Deteriorating; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: High.

Methodology Applied:

  • A composite absolute value between 0.60 and 0.75 indicates transition risk and imminent regime change (1).
  • Confirmation of a regime requires the composite to maintain a threshold (e.g., > 0.75) for two consecutive months (1).
  • Recent observations (1–2 months) should be discounted due to high revision risk in weekly H.8 data (1).
  • Private Credit Impulse Signal (Latest: 2026-05-31) (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the bank credit component (TOTBKCR), with a z-score of 0.73, while other components remain unreleased for the latest period (1).
  • A sharp deceleration from April’s 1.66 to May’s 0.73 suggests a loss of credit momentum (1).
  • Internal Conflict: The "Stable" label is triggered by the latest print, but missing business and consumer loan data creates high uncertainty (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: A revision or subsequent print pushing the composite back above 0.75 would re-establish the "Accelerating" regime.

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Stabilization near long-term trends as credit expansion cools.
  • Upside risk: Re-acceleration of business lending demand if funding conditions ease further.
  • Downside risk: Broadening deceleration into a "Risk-off" contraction if consumer credit momentum fails.

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Cyclical (months), as credit impulses typically lead broader economic shifts (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: Low, due to incomplete data in the latest two periods and high revision sensitivity (1).

Macro Relevance:

  • Informs the demand and liquidity dimensions by tracking the rate of private sector debt creation (1).
  • The move toward the transition zone implies a potential cooling of the previously easier financing environment (1).
  • Cycle position: Not determined.
  • Typically confirms GDP growth signals; divergence would suggest nominal distortions or securitization shifts (1).

Regime Context:

  • Recently exited a two-month "Accelerating" peak (March–April) to enter a "Stable" classification in May (1).
  • Direction of change: Weakening.

Model Limitations:

  • High revision risk in H.8 source data and potential distortions from high inflation periods (1).

Data & References:

  • Private Credit Impulse Signal (2026-05-31) (1).
  • Most influential: TOTBKCR (z-score 0.73) and previous peak impulse (1.66) (1).
  • U.S. CPI/PCE inflation and Fed Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS).
Financial Stress Index Signal

Signal Summary:

  • Configuration statement: Given STLFSI4 at -0.7621 and a Stress_z of -0.528, this setup aligns with Upward-biased price paths and Compressed volatility, where the dominant risk is Regime shift, not Mean reversion (1).
  • The signal has entered a Bullish/Risk-on regime as both the raw index and z-score satisfy the methodology's expansionary thresholds (1).
  • Conviction Band: Medium; Interpretation Confidence: High Confidence; Internal Conflict Flag: No. Signal Stability Assessment: Improving; Threshold Proximity: Near; Revision Sensitivity: Unknown.

Methodology Applied:

  • STLFSI4 < 0 and Stress_z < -0.5 defines a Bullish regime reflecting loose financial conditions (1).
  • STLFSI4 > 0 or Stress_z > +0.5 triggers a Bearish regime indicating systemic financial stress (1).
  • Financial Stress Index Signal: latest observation dated 2026-05-08 (1).

Key Dynamics:

  • The primary driver is the decline in STLFSI4 to -0.7621, the lowest level in the provided history (1).
  • Momentum is positive as the Stress_z has improved from Bearish levels (1.62) in March to Bullish levels (-0.52) in May (1).
  • Internal tensions are absent, but the signal shows recent whipsaw behavior around the -0.5 threshold (1).
  • Conditional Invalidation: Stress_z rising above the -0.5 threshold, reverting the signal to Neutral (1).

Scenario Balance:

  • Base case dominant: Bullish regime persistence driven by below-normal stress and high intermediation capacity (1).
  • Upside risk: Sustained Bullish regime if STLFSI4 continues to diverge negatively from historical stress norms (1).
  • Downside risk: Sudden transition to Neutral if interbank funding or credit spreads spike unexpectedly (1).

Time Horizon & Aggregation:

  • Time Horizon: Tactical (weeks) because the signal is derived from a weekly series with high sensitivity to market shifts (1).
  • Aggregation Weight Hint: High, as systemic stress is a foundational filter for cyclical risk-taking (1).

Macro Relevance:

  • This signal informs the liquidity and risk aversion dimensions of the macro environment (1).
  • The downward direction implies an expansionary transmission mechanism through improved interbank funding and lower credit premiums (1).
  • Cycle position: not determined.

Regime Context:

  • The signal recently transitioned from a persistent Bearish state (Feb-Mar) to a fragile Bullish regime (1).
  • The direction of change is strengthening as financial tightness continues to dissipate (1).

Model Limitations:

  • Potential data staleness in sub-components like interbank funding spreads (1).
  • Whipsaw risk is elevated when Stress_z is near the 0.5 or -0.5 thresholds (1).

Data & References:

  • Financial Stress Index Signal (latest: 2026-05-08) (1).
  • Dominant datapoints: STLFSI4 (-0.7621) and Stress_z (-0.5287) (1).
  • Corporate High Yield OAS and the VIX would provide additional depth to this signal.
